newsitem.title: USA: American General expects to cut 1,200 jobs.
newsitem.headline: American General expects to cut 1,200 jobs.

text.p: American General Corp said Thursday it expects to eliminate about 1,200 jobs beginning in the third quarter as a result of its merger with USLIFE Corp.

"Severance and related costs of $34 million relate to the elimination of approximately 1,200 positions beginning in third quarter 1997," the company said in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission regarding its second quarter performance.
The Houston-based insurance and financial services giant said the layoffs would be part of its restructuring after its $1.8 billion acquisition of USLIFE Corp, which was completed in June.

"The positions to be eliminated relate to USLIFE's corporate operations and to administrative service functions that will be centralized within the Independent Producer division," American General said in the filing.

The company also said that as a result of the acquisition, it recorded $37 million in costs during the second quarter related to closing "redundant facilities" and write-offs of mainframe computer equipment and related software at locations that will be centralized.
